name: Hodaviah
overview: Hodaviah was a male member of the tribe of Asher, identified specifically as the son of Zophah. His mention in Scripture is brief and primarily genealogical, with no additional notes expanding on his life or role. As the third individual named Hodaviah in the biblical record, he is distinguished by his paternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Hodaviah means "grandeur," though it is not indicated that this name was given by God. This single recorded name provides a straightforward identification without further titles or descriptive meanings.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hodaviah as the son of Zophah. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hodaviah's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the tribe of Asher, serving as a link in the lineage that preserves the heritage of Israel. His mention underscores the importance of family lines in the biblical narrative, even when individual details are scarce. While not highlighted for specific deeds or roles, his inclusion reflects God's providential care in maintaining the identity of His people through generations.
